The aim is to reduce human input in coordinating and monitoring multiple AI agents, according to a paper published by the company’s DeepSeek Harness team and reported by Singapore’s South China Morning Post on Sunday. Managing multiple agents demands human attention, the team said, noting that “single-task limits depend on model capabilities, while multitask limits depend on human attention.” The DeepSeek paper said a person can oversee only three to five active AI agent sessions simultaneously. Its proposed system would distribute tasks among agents and coordinate their work, leaving humans free to review results and make decisions. The proposal comes amid intense competition among AI developers, including US companies Anthropic and OpenAI, according to the SCMP. Cointelegraph reported last October that Chinese artificial intelligence models were outperforming US counterparts in cryptocurrency trading, according to data from blockchain analytics platform CoinGlass. AI chatbot DeepSeek led a crypto trading experiment, being the only AI model to generate a positive unrealized return of 9.1%. DeepSeek said that advances in AI models have sparked the emergence of agents that can streamline a diverse array of workflows, from managing calendars and handling professional correspondence to technical reporting and software development. Reuters-Yonhap News - Seoul Economic Daily International News from South Korea](https://wimg.sedaily.com/news/cms/2026/11/01/rcv.YNA.20261019.PRU20261019344201009_P1.jpg "DeepSeek Unveils 'Super Agent' to Run Multiple Tasks at Once") The DeepSeek logo is projected onto a computer keyboard. Reuters-Yonhap News Chinese artificial intelligence firm DeepSeek has unveiled a new architecture called "Super Agent" that deploys multiple AI agents to carry out a range of tasks simultaneously. According to Global Times and Lianhe Zaobao on the 1st, DeepSeek said a day earlier that Super Agent is not confined to a single chat window and can continuously handle multiple assignments while proactively responding to changes in its environment. DeepSeek said the number of tasks AI can perform keeps growing, but the human attention needed to manage them has not expanded at the same pace, creating a bottleneck in productivity gains. One person can manage only three to five conversations at the same time, the company said. Super Agent is designed so that the system, rather than a person, handles conversation management and context synchronization. Humans set goals and review results, while the AI coordinates and executes the work. The architecture is built around routers and workers that collaborate like a virtual team. A router gathers information in bulk from multiple platforms such as chat and email and distributes assignments, while workers carry out individual tasks such as code review and feature development. As a result, users communicate with a single AI agent, but multiple agents are actually performing the work at the same time. DeepSeek said Super Agent also has the initiative to identify problems and propose solutions without separate instructions. For example, it can monitor conversations in a group chat room, recognize an issue on its own when one is raised and suggest ways to resolve it. Still, DeepSeek said Super Agent is not based on a new theory, but applies design concepts from existing computing systems to AI agent architecture. highlights.content: #### Tomorrow's Affairs GET - On the App Store ![TOMORROW'S AFFAIRS](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/assets/img/logo.svg) #### Analysis of today - Assessment of tomorrow ![TOMORROW'S AFFAIRS](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/assets/img/logo.svg) ![TOMORROW'S AFFAIRS](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/assets/img/logo.svg) #### Analysis of today - Assessment of tomorrow ![TOMORROW'S AFFAIRS](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/assets/img/logo.svg) ![Software Developer](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/image/news/image/8884/1/0/0/Software+Developer+EDITED.jpg) # Who is controlling the AI agent when things go wrong? In May this year, when I wrote about [rogue AI agents](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/rogue-ai-agents-do-we-value-speed-above-caution), I questioned whether we were prioritising speed over prudence. I was concerned that although technology was developing quickly, the security conversation was lagging behind. We are still too focused on what AI can achieve. Every week brings new announcements about autonomous agents, digital workers, intelligent automation, and systems that can complete highly complex tasks with minimal human involvement. Businesses want productivity gains, technology companies want market share, and investors want to identify the next major opportunity. Yet we still do not ask one question often enough: who is controlling the AI agent when things go wrong? ### **The challenge with trusting AI judgment** Traditional software generally follows predefined instructions. AI agents operate differently. They interpret objectives, develop plans, select tools, make decisions, and execute sequences of actions, changing the security equation. Although AI agents operate based within the permissions they are granted, they often struggle to recognise the limits of their own authority. Risks can range from generating flawed outputs to compromising data by altering security configurations, or deleting critical information This can cause them to misinterpret instructions, overextend goals, respond unpredictably to external data, or execute tasks in unintended ways. When these system errors have real-world consequences, risks can range from generating flawed outputs to compromising data by altering security configurations, or deleting critical information. ### **The incidents we need to pay attention to** Last month, the UK published details of [incidents](https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/incident-report-unsanctioned-agent-behaviour-during-cyber-testing) involving advanced AI agents during testing and development. These incidents included systems that circumvented technical controls, accessed real-world systems beyond their intended environment, and established unintended communication channels with other agents. In one case, agents coordinated through external channels on a scale involving hundreds of agents over several days. Although these were controlled evaluations designed to test model capabilities (which we need to improve the systems), and some safeguards had deliberately been reduced, the incidents confirmed how easily autonomous systems can exceed their intended boundaries when technical controls fail. Stronger security practices, tighter technical restrictions, and comprehensive monitoring could have prevented many of these incidents. And this is precisely the point. We do not need to wait for a major disaster to recognise the importance of security architecture. AI safety guardrails need to be a top priority. Another example came from Anthropic. highlights.content: ![Bei Akademie registrieren](/images/banner_desktop_1110x150.webp) ![ad-hoc-news.de](/img/logos/ad-hoc-news.svg) # [BÖRSE](/boerse/news) # [BÖRSE](/boerse/news) ![Logo ad-hoc-news.de](/img/logos/ad-hoc-news.svg) # Micro-Star International stock expands its AI infrastructure push ## AI Infrastructure Broadens MSI's Reach ![MSI, TW0002377009, Illustration mit AI erstellt.](https://mdb.ad-hoc-news.de/bild/bild-2405025_1200_0.webp) Micro-Star International presented a broader AI infrastructure portfolio at the OCP Global Summit on October 13, 2026. According to [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/msi-showcases-open-data-center-and-ai-infrastructure-at-2026-ocp-global-summit-ce785dd2db89f620 "MarketScreener report on MSI at the 2026 OCP Global Summit"), the company showcased 21-inch ORv3 systems, DC-MHS modular platforms, NVIDIA MGX rack and server solutions, and the XpertStation WS300 desktop AI supercomputer. The presentation gives investors a view of MSI's push beyond traditional gaming and PC components. Its infrastructure lineup is designed to cover different deployment sizes, from local AI development to high-density data center workloads. ## From Modular Servers To Desktop AI MSI's ORv3 portfolio includes two-node systems in air-cooled and direct-liquid-cooled configurations. The company also presented a 48-rack-unit NVIDIA MGX configuration built from liquid-cooled servers, networking equipment and management switches. The XpertStation WS300 extends the same strategy to the desktop. The system uses NVIDIA's GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip and supports local AI model prototyping, fine-tuning and inference. Two units can be clustered for larger workloads, according to the MarketScreener report. For investors, the product mix points to an attempt to capture AI infrastructure spending across several layers rather than relying only on consumer PC demand. Commercial adoption, customer orders and the pace of data center investment remain important factors for the outlook. ## MSI's Business And Competitive Position MSI is a Taiwan-based computer hardware company that manufactures and distributes motherboards, graphics cards, notebooks, monitors, servers, industrial computers and related consumer electronics. Its products are sold mainly in Taiwan, Europe, other parts of Asia and the Americas, according to the company profile published by MarketScreener and [MSI](https://www.msi.com/about/investor "MSI investor information"). In PC components and gaming hardware, MSI competes with Taiwan-based ASUSTeK Computer and Gigabyte. MSI is positioned as a diversified specialist that combines consumer hardware with a growing server and AI infrastructure offering, while its rivals have similarly broad positions across PC components and systems. ### Micro-Star International At A Glance Regional technology shares remain sensitive to demand for computing hardware and AI infrastructure; see [Current market reports](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/marktberichte/). The aim is to reduce human input in coordinating and monitoring multiple AI agents, according to a paper published by the company’s DeepSeek Harness team and reported by Singapore’s South China Morning Post on Sunday. Managing multiple agents demands human attention, the team said, noting that “single-task limits depend on model capabilities, while multitask limits depend on human attention.” The DeepSeek paper said a person can oversee only three to five active AI agent sessions simultaneously. Its proposed system would distribute tasks among agents and coordinate their work, leaving humans free to review results and make decisions. The proposal comes amid intense competition among AI developers, including US companies Anthropic and OpenAI, according to the SCMP. Cointelegraph reported last October that Chinese artificial intelligence models were outperforming US counterparts in cryptocurrency trading, according to data from blockchain analytics platform CoinGlass. AI chatbot DeepSeek led a crypto trading experiment, being the only AI model to generate a positive unrealized return of 9.1%. The results surprised crypto traders, given that DeepSeek was developed at a fraction of the cost of its US rivals. ***Magazine: New DeepSeek ban in US, Swiss-Asia crypto ties deepen: Asia Express*** ## Compare charts ## [Latest news](/news-flow) ## [More news from Cointelegraph](/news-flow/?provider=cointelegraph) Select market data provided by [ICE Data Services](https://www.ice.com/fixed-income-data-services). The primary motive behind the proposed system, is aimed at mitigating the need for humans to coordinate multiple AI agents and track their advancement resolving a major constraint in administering today’s increasingly intricate operations. DeepSeek said that advances in AI models have sparked the emergence of agents that can streamline a diverse array of workflows, from managing calendars and handling professional correspondence to technical reporting and software development. The recent initiative comes as competition has escalated among AI developers to develop more autonomous coding assistants with Anthropic’s Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex demonstrating advanced proficiency in managing intricate development pipelines. According to some industry experts, DeepSeek was making progress in the right direction but questioned whether the proposal offered substantial improvements over existing systems. DeepSeek conceded inherent risks regarding data protection and confidentiality; moreover recently the company released an open-source prototype of the super-agent on the code-hosting platform GitHub, while clarifying that the project was merely a structural proof of concept rather than a fully developed offering. ![Ruqia Shahid](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/reporters/8610_110959_reporter.jpg) Ruqia Shahid is a reporter specialising in science, focusing on discoveries, research developments, and technological advancements. Reuters-Yonhap News - Seoul Economic Daily International News from South Korea](https://wimg.sedaily.com/news/cms/2026/11/01/rcv.YNA.20261019.PRU20261019344201009_P1.jpg "DeepSeek Unveils 'Super Agent' to Run Multiple Tasks at Once") The DeepSeek logo is projected onto a computer keyboard. Reuters-Yonhap News Chinese artificial intelligence firm DeepSeek has unveiled a new architecture called "Super Agent" that deploys multiple AI agents to carry out a range of tasks simultaneously. According to Global Times and Lianhe Zaobao on the 1st, DeepSeek said a day earlier that Super Agent is not confined to a single chat window and can continuously handle multiple assignments while proactively responding to changes in its environment. DeepSeek said the number of tasks AI can perform keeps growing, but the human attention needed to manage them has not expanded at the same pace, creating a bottleneck in productivity gains. One person can manage only three to five conversations at the same time, the company said. Super Agent is designed so that the system, rather than a person, handles conversation management and context synchronization. Humans set goals and review results, while the AI coordinates and executes the work. The architecture is built around routers and workers that collaborate like a virtual team. A router gathers information in bulk from multiple platforms such as chat and email and distributes assignments, while workers carry out individual tasks such as code review and feature development. As a result, users communicate with a single AI agent, but multiple agents are actually performing the work at the same time. DeepSeek said Super Agent also has the initiative to identify problems and propose solutions without separate instructions. For example, it can monitor conversations in a group chat room, recognize an issue on its own when one is raised and suggest ways to resolve it. Still, DeepSeek said Super Agent is not based on a new theory, but applies design concepts from existing computing systems to AI agent architecture. AI Agents.content: #### Tomorrow's Affairs GET - On the App Store ![TOMORROW'S AFFAIRS](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/assets/img/logo.svg) #### Analysis of today - Assessment of tomorrow ![TOMORROW'S AFFAIRS](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/assets/img/logo.svg) ![TOMORROW'S AFFAIRS](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/assets/img/logo.svg) #### Analysis of today - Assessment of tomorrow ![TOMORROW'S AFFAIRS](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/assets/img/logo.svg) ![Software Developer](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/image/news/image/8884/1/0/0/Software+Developer+EDITED.jpg) # Who is controlling the AI agent when things go wrong? In May this year, when I wrote about [rogue AI agents](https://tomorrowsaffairs.com/rogue-ai-agents-do-we-value-speed-above-caution), I questioned whether we were prioritising speed over prudence. I was concerned that although technology was developing quickly, the security conversation was lagging behind. We are still too focused on what AI can achieve. Every week brings new announcements about autonomous agents, digital workers, intelligent automation, and systems that can complete highly complex tasks with minimal human involvement. Businesses want productivity gains, technology companies want market share, and investors want to identify the next major opportunity. Yet we still do not ask one question often enough: who is controlling the AI agent when things go wrong? ### **The challenge with trusting AI judgment** Traditional software generally follows predefined instructions. AI agents operate differently. They interpret objectives, develop plans, select tools, make decisions, and execute sequences of actions, changing the security equation. Although AI agents operate based within the permissions they are granted, they often struggle to recognise the limits of their own authority. Risks can range from generating flawed outputs to compromising data by altering security configurations, or deleting critical information This can cause them to misinterpret instructions, overextend goals, respond unpredictably to external data, or execute tasks in unintended ways. When these system errors have real-world consequences, risks can range from generating flawed outputs to compromising data by altering security configurations, or deleting critical information. ### **The incidents we need to pay attention to** Last month, the UK published details of [incidents](https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/incident-report-unsanctioned-agent-behaviour-during-cyber-testing) involving advanced AI agents during testing and development. These incidents included systems that circumvented technical controls, accessed real-world systems beyond their intended environment, and established unintended communication channels with other agents. In one case, agents coordinated through external channels on a scale involving hundreds of agents over several days. Although these were controlled evaluations designed to test model capabilities (which we need to improve the systems), and some safeguards had deliberately been reduced, the incidents confirmed how easily autonomous systems can exceed their intended boundaries when technical controls fail. Stronger security practices, tighter technical restrictions, and comprehensive monitoring could have prevented many of these incidents. And this is precisely the point. We do not need to wait for a major disaster to recognise the importance of security architecture. AI safety guardrails need to be a top priority. Another example came from Anthropic. In September, the company disclosed four incidents in which [Claude models](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-anthropic-fourth-ai-hacking-incident-20260/) gained unauthorised access to real third-party systems during cybersecurity evaluations. What happens when the system responsible for performing a task can also interfere with the mechanisms designed to supervise it? AI Agents.content: # DeepSeek unveils super agent coordinating multiple AIs for parallel tasks By  [Lee Ho-jun](https://biz.chosun.com/en/people/lee-hojun/) Published 2026.11.01. 20:34 [Prefer Chosunbiz EN on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=biz.chosun.com) DeepSeek logo. /Courtesy of Yonhap News According to Global Times and Lianhe Zaobao on the 1st (local time), Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) corporations DeepSeek on the previous day announced a new architecture, "super agent," that deploys AI agents to perform multiple tasks simultaneously. DeepSeek noted that while the tasks AI can handle are rapidly increasing, human attention has limits. It said a person can usually manage only three to five conversations at the same time, making it difficult to fully leverage AI productivity. Super agent overcomes these limits by having the system, not people, handle conversation management and context synchronization. People set goals and review final results, while AI handles task coordination and execution. In super agent, a "coordinator" (router) and an "executor" (worker) operate like a virtual team. The router ingests platform information such as chats and emails in bulk and assigns tasks, and the worker performs each task, such as code review and feature development. As a result, users interact with a single AI agent, but in practice multiple agents work simultaneously. The company said super agent is proactive, monitoring conversations in group chat rooms and independently recognizing raised issues and offering solutions even without separate instructions. DeepSeek said the technology is not an entirely new theory and that it applies the task distribution and information processing methods of existing computing systems to an AI architecture. ※ This article has been translated by AI. Mistral Large 4 weights were released Oct. 29. See the vLLM example, the license’s MaaS condition, and how API rates differ from benchmark task cost. Mistral announced the release of Mistral Large 4’s downloadable weights on October 29, 2026, moving the model from its public-preview stage toward self-hosting. The preview was listed on October 6; NeoTeo covered it in its [report on the public preview](https://www.neoteo.com/en/mistral-ai-opens-public-preview-of-mistral-large-4). The weights are available under a license with a specific condition for some commercial deployments. ## What the released checkpoint supports Amine AI’s Mistral Large 4 prompt comparison The Hugging Face checkpoint is named `mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B`; Mistral’s API model name is `mistral-large-4`. The model accepts text and images and returns text, with a stated context window of 1 million tokens. Mistral describes it as a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with about 1.05 trillion total parameters. Its model card counts 49 billion active parameters per token when embeddings and output layers are excluded, or 52 billion when they are included. [Mistral’s model card](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B) Amine AI’s October 30 video includes a creator-made prompt comparison between Mistral Large 4 and Claude Opus 5.5, alongside screens showing model cards and benchmark graphs. ## What Mistral’s vLLM example specifies Mistral’s published vLLM example sets `--tensor-parallel-size 8`. Tensor parallelism splits model computation across processors; this setting describes the example, not a stated minimum GPU count. ET Government reported on November 1, 2026 that the country’s state-backed AI push is moving away from building foundation models and toward real-world applications for Bharat, with BharatGen’s Ganesh Ramakrishnan among the voices shaping that turn. The shift matters because the first phase of the IndiaAI Mission, a ₹10,371.92 crore programme approved in 2024, has now produced working models. The open question is whether anyone will use them at scale. The pieces are in place. Sarvam AI has open-sourced 30B and 105B parameter models, BharatGen has launched a 17B Mixture of Experts model for 22 languages, and Gnani.ai has shipped speech-native systems. Public language tooling is also maturing, as our earlier report on [CIIL’s Anuvani open speech AI for 22 Indian languages](https://shattered.io/ciil-anuvani-open-source-speech-ai-22-indian-languages-2026/) showed. This analysis lays out what is confirmed, what the money and compute look like, and where the real test sits for the next 12 months. One note on sourcing before we start. We could not retrieve the full ET Government text for this piece, so we paraphrase its framing and lean on separate, named coverage for every figure below. Where outlets disagree, we use the more conservative number and say so. No direct quotes appear in this article because we have no verified verbatim statements to reproduce. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. Can the country train its own large language models? By early 2026 the answer was yes. AI Product.content: [![Straitstimes.com header logo](/assets/ST-logo-default-aoeSLh4S.png)](https://www.straitstimes.com) # AI doesn’t destroy art but raises the bar for even better content creation, says Adobe APAC chief [Sign up now:](/newsletter-signup?ref=inline-article) Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox Ben Goodman, president of Adobe Asia-Pacific and Japan, says the flood of AI content will only make audiences more discerning. ST PHOTO: GIN TAY [![avatar-alt](https://cassette.sphdigital.com.sg/image/straitstimes/eb8b2cc8719c8f564932ce08c4cd14df5fb21aa80f53f35145b46c4193197fc3?w=150) Benjamin Lim](/authors/benjamin-lim?ref=article-byline) Published Nov 02, 2026, 05:00 AM Updated Nov 02, 2026, 05:00 AM * Adobe says AI raises content standards, not destroys art, because audiences now spot poor work and demand better, more personalised marketing. * The company is expanding from creative software into AI and data tools, including Sensei, Firefly and CX Enterprise Coworker, to speed up campaigns and improve customer insights. * Adobe says Singapore is a key hub for AI growth, citing strong adoption, local examples like STB and Chow Tai Fook, and a 2025 deal with HTX on content authenticity. AI generated SINGAPORE – Extra fingers. Illegible text. Facial features that look eerily symmetrical. These are the telltale signs of [AI-generated visuals](/tech/can-you-spot-the-ai-generated-images?ref=inline-article) that you may spot in an advertisement poster or social media post today. These common mistakes are fuelling negative sentiment about AI among the creative community, with many perceiving the drastically increased accessibility to graphic design and content creation more as a bane than a boon. AI Product.content: CFOtech Asia - Technology news for CFOs & financial decision-makers [![CFOtech Asia logo](/brands/cfo-new-logo.svg)](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.asia) ![Dayforce launches agentic HCM platform with native AI](https://cfotech.asia/uploads/story/2026/11/02/david-ossip-story-323195.webp) [HCM](https://cfotech.asia/tag/human-capital-management) [ERP](https://cfotech.asia/tag/enterprise-resource-planning) [Data Privacy](https://cfotech.asia/tag/data-privacy) # Dayforce launches agentic HCM platform with native AI Mon, 2nd Nov 2026 (Today) [![Sean Mitchell](https://cfotech.asia/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyOSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--a929a91c2a04d9af95ed98b14ed4d405bc70c1a7/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/IMG_3092.webp) SEAN MITCHELL Publisher](/author/sean-mitchell) Dayforce has launched its Agentic HCM Platform, adding native AI across its human capital management system. The launch marks a broader overhaul of the Dayforce platform, with new tools for recruiting, workforce management, payroll, planning and HR administration, alongside a new set of AI-driven services. At the centre of the platform is what Dayforce describes as a single foundation for identity, permissions, privacy, security, approvals and auditability. These controls are intended to govern a shift from AI systems that answer questions to systems that can carry out tasks. Dayforce has built the offer around several components: Ask Dayforce, a conversational interface that runs across the platform; Dayforce AI Agents, a portfolio of specialised tools designed to handle multi-step work; and Dayforce Bots, which customers can create to automate recurring or event-driven processes. It also introduced Dayforce Build, which lets users create apps, bots and documents in plain language without coding. Dayforce Marketplace will serve as a distribution channel for pre-built apps and bots from Dayforce, partners and customers, while Dayforce Build Academy is intended to provide training and certification for users who want to publish those tools. Another part of the update focuses on integration with third-party systems. The software will be available through channels such as instant messaging tools and SMS, while plugins and connectors will allow Dayforce data and actions to work with external AI assistants and business systems, including through expanded partnerships with Microsoft and Anthropic's Claude. Implementation is also part of the announcement. Dayforce Deploy is a new AI-based implementation workspace that links requirements, configuration and testing, with the aim of reducing manual work and identifying issues earlier in deployment projects. Alongside the platform changes, Dayforce outlined updates across its business software. In talent management, it is releasing a new recruiting product that combines customer relationship management, high-volume workflows, contingent staffing coordination and AI agents. Ribbon AI technology will be integrated into that experience to add sourcing, rediscovery, voice and video interviews, and candidate insights. The workforce management and pay side of the business is also being updated. Dayforce Command Centre for Frontline Operations is designed to give managers a single view across recruiting, onboarding, scheduling and time, while new scheduling and manager time tools are intended to help address coverage and exceptions across teams and sites. Dayforce is also adding contingent workforce management features for supplier oversight, labour rates, approvals, invoicing and supplier performance, as well as a redesigned payroll experience for teams running Dayforce Payroll across countries. But pallet companies are mining data from their processes and are improving them thanks to cameras and other AI solutions offered by Zira ([www.zira.us](http://www.zira.us)). A camera with AI is different. Show it a finished pallet and it counts pallets. Show it a protruding nail and it checks for them. Show it a running machine and it tells you when the machine stops. The hardware barely changes. What changes is what you teach it. The owner’s question shifts from “What sensor do I need to install?” to “What do I want to know?” This matters in pallets because nearly everything important in a plant happens out in the open: boards, nails, stacks, people, forklifts and trucks. The reality is that when measured numbers replace estimates, they often don’t match what everyone assumed. Held at the Rosewood Commons Conference Center, TechBeat 2026 focused on developments in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, robotics, humanoid technology and enterprise AI. The event aimed to create opportunities for startups to connect with potential buyers, business leaders and investors rather than function as a conventional technology exhibition. One of the key attractions was a humanoid robot that interacted with attendees, offering them a closer look at the possibilities of human-machine interaction. Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology also drew attention during the event. The conference followed an unconventional format, with presentations and discussions taking place across different halls. Instead of keeping participants in a single auditorium throughout the day, organizers encouraged them to move between venues after each session. Sunny Menon, the founder and driving force behind TechBeat, announced the transitions, while volunteers helped guide attendees. Startup development remained central to this year’s edition. Continuing an initiative from previous years, TechBeat selected SunnySide.AI, an emerging startup from India, as its adopted and fostered venture for 2026. SunnySide.AI operates in the sales enablement and go-to-market space, offering a platform designed to help businesses improve sales execution and expand their market reach. Through the initiative, TechBeat aims to help selected startups gain visibility, build business relationships, connect with potential customers and work towards sustainable growth. Another interesting session featured author, poet, actor and producer Thampy Antony Thekkek, who shared his views on artificial intelligence from the perspective of a creative writer. Speaking beside an exhibition of his published books, Antony discussed his preference for writing through his own creative consciousness rather than depending on AI to produce his work. Menon explained that TechBeat was created to offer something different from conventional business and technology gatherings. “At most conferences, people often find themselves standing alone in a crowd where everyone is trying to sell something. We wanted to create something different. Our objective is to bring sellers and buyers into a meaningful synchrony, while giving promising startups the opportunity to be seen, heard and supported. We want to help take these ventures forward, not simply give them a platform for one day,” he said. Menon said the conference was intended to build an ecosystem where startups could connect with established businesses and enterprise decision-makers. “TechBeat is about creating an ecosystem where fresh ideas can meet experience, where startups can connect with enterprise decision makers, and where people can find opportunities to collaborate. We want these connections to continue long after the conference concludes.” The event also attracted interest from attendees who expressed their willingness to...

Anyone running the tool that strips refusals from AI models has homework before it works again.* If you have a Heretic 1.x configuration file sitting around, it won't run anymore. Heretic, the open-source tool that automates the removal of refusal behavior from AI language models, shipped version 2.0.0 on November 1, according to its GitHub release page. The update is a breaking change, and the project says anyone upgrading needs to follow a migration guide before their old setups work again. The headline change is something called Arbitrary-Rank Ablation, or ARA, which replaces the dense-weight method Heretic used in its earlier versions. Instead of directly editing a model's full weight matrices to erase its "refusal direction," the internal pattern that makes a model say "I can't help with that," ARA computes the same adjustment through a low-rank update. In plain terms, it does less math to get the same result, which the release notes tie to faster runs and broader model compatibility. Twenty contributors touched this release, 11 of them for the first time, which says something about how fast the project has built a community willing to write code for it rather than just download the output. Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [![ITWire](/brand/itwire-logo-template.ad986f71.png) Australian for tech news](/) Advertisement [Business It News / Business Intelligence](/business-it-news/business-intelligence) # How open source AI agents, skills, and MCP servers are reshaping cybersecurity defense [Kirsten Doyle](/tag/kirsten-doyle/) | ![How open source AI agents, skills, and MCP servers are reshaping cybersecurity defense](https://media.itwire.com/2026/11/01/how-open-source-ai-agents-skills-and-mcp-servers-are-reshaping-cybersecurity-defense-004d3df94f75.jpg) Business Intelligence The model is the easy part of an AI agent With the advancement of large language models (LLMs) and artificial intelligence (AI) agents in recent years, building effective [AI tooling for cybersecurity teams](https://www.tenable.com/press-releases/tenable-launches-industrys-first-open-source-ai-agent-exchange) is becoming drastically easier. But getting them to work safely and consistently with the security tools you already run is still no easy task. Picture what a vulnerability management team wants from an agent: pull findings from three scanners, check each asset against threat intelligence, work out which fix removes the most risk, and drop the answer into the ticketing queue. Every step touches a different system. If each connection needs its own integration, you’ve built a maintenance burden before the agent does anything useful. That’s the problem open source AI agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and reusable skills are starting to solve. They let security teams standardize those connections and reuse work someone else has already done and published. The large language model (LLM) behind the agent is only one part of the system, and increasingly it’s the least differentiated part. Advertisement The large language model (LLM) behind the agent is only one part of that system. **Why does MCP matter to security teams?** [MCP is an open standard](https://itwire.com/business-it-news/data/elastic-delivers-first-embedded-ai-experiences-for-observability-and-security-inside-third-party-ai-tools) for connecting AI applications to external tools and data sources. For security teams, its value rests on a fact of life: no security environment comes from one vendor. An agent working on even a single vulnerability might need to reach: •   Vulnerability scanners •   Cloud platforms •   Identity systems •   Code security tools •   Ticketing systems •   Threat intelligence feeds •   Asset inventories Without a common protocol, each of those is a bespoke integration, and it breaks the moment you introduce a second agent or swap the underlying model. An MCP server exposes a tool’s capabilities through one consistent interface. Any agent that speaks the protocol can use them, and nobody rebuilds the connection per agent. The practical payoff is choice. You decide how agents connect to your tooling, rather than inheriting whatever integration layer a single supplier ships. Vendor-neutral isn’t a feature, it’s the whole point. **How are agentic skills different from MCP servers?** An MCP server connects an agent to a tool. A skill tells the agent how to do a job. The distinction matters because the two are reusable separately. Take vulnerability prioritization. An MCP server gives the agent access to vulnerability and asset data. A skill holds the instructions the agent follows to analyze that data and decide which remediation actions come first. Any agent that picks up the skill inherits the process, and a team that swaps its scanner keeps the skill and changes only the server. Typically, these improvements are witnessed in driver updates, but [Snapdragon X2 Elite](https://wccftech.com/snapdragon-x2-elite-family-announced-with-the-chipset-versions/) users are reporting the complete opposite: steep performance drops after updating to Qualcomm’s latest Adreno GPU driver, with two separate posts pointing to version 32.0.181.0 as the culprit. The reports involve different workloads, one in video editing and the other in local AI, but both appeared within days of each other. ## LLM performance in open-source AI models like Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct dropped to just 5.9 tokens per second The first post comes from Redditor ‘u/FullTimePedestrian’, who [claims](https://www.reddit.com/r/snapdragon/comments/1xjpip3/if_you_use_premiere_do_not_update_gpu_to_v3201810/) that his Zenbook A16 suffered a massive rendering performance dip in Adobe Premiere Pro, and warned users not to update to version 32.0.181.0. Without saving any proof, he states that a 7-minute 1080p video that previously rendered in just 1 minute and 40 seconds now takes around 10 minutes, which is roughly six times longer. The user also notes that editing programs always seem to run into issues after a new driver release. [##### **Related Story** NUVIA Co-Founder Gerard Williams Takes A Possible Veiled Jab At Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, Saying “Real Progress Isn’t Just About Pushing Frequencies Higher”](https://wccftech.com/gerard-williams-snapdragon-dig-real-progress-not-higher-frequencies/) As for the more comprehensive performance drop, that was experienced by user ‘u/NonVeganLasVegan’, who says that the Snapdragon X2 Elite powering Microsoft’s Surface Laptop 8th Edition and paired with the Adreno X2-85 GPU saw local LLM text generation through llama.cpp’s OpenCL backend became 69 to 87 percent slower after moving from driver 32.0.172.2 to 32.0.181.0. The graph also reveals that the Snapdragon X2 Elite was tested on Qwen3-0.6B, dropping from 98.1 to 12.8 tokens per second, with Qwen3-4B dropping from 29.5 to 9.0, and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct dropping from 26.8 to 5.9 tokens per second. The poster says the laptop, software, models, and operating system stayed the same, and the system was plugged in. Open Source AI.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) # Sovereign AI in India Shifts to Apps: 20 Models [2026] ![Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/tvance.webp) [Tom Vance](https://shattered.io/author/tvance/) Updated Nov 1, 2026 · 15 min read Sovereign AI in India has entered a new phase. ET Government reported on November 1, 2026 that the country’s state-backed AI push is moving away from building foundation models and toward real-world applications for Bharat, with BharatGen’s Ganesh Ramakrishnan among the voices shaping that turn. The shift matters because the first phase of the IndiaAI Mission, a ₹10,371.92 crore programme approved in 2024, has now produced working models. The open question is whether anyone will use them at scale. The pieces are in place. Sarvam AI has open-sourced 30B and 105B parameter models, BharatGen has launched a 17B Mixture of Experts model for 22 languages, and Gnani.ai has shipped speech-native systems. Public language tooling is also maturing, as our earlier report on [CIIL’s Anuvani open speech AI for 22 Indian languages](https://shattered.io/ciil-anuvani-open-source-speech-ai-22-indian-languages-2026/) showed. This analysis lays out what is confirmed, what the money and compute look like, and where the real test sits for the next 12 months. One note on sourcing before we start. We could not retrieve the full ET Government text for this piece, so we paraphrase its framing and lean on separate, named coverage for every figure below. Where outlets disagree, we use the more conservative number and say so. No direct quotes appear in this article because we have no verified verbatim statements to reproduce. ![shattered.io](https://shattered.io/static/favicon.svg)· Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions. Can the country train its own large language models? By early 2026 the answer was yes. Sarvam AI announced and open-sourced two models in February, and the government told Parliament it was funding a dozen organisations to build indigenous foundation models. That answer changes the question. A model that scores well on a benchmark does nothing for a farmer in Vidarbha or a clerk processing land records in Gujarat. The new test is deployment. Who builds the interface, who pays for inference, who checks accuracy in Marathi or Odia, and who is liable when the answer is wrong? Policy commentators were already saying this in February. A Policy Circle opinion piece on the India AI Impact Summit argued that deployment mattered more than slogans. Business Standard and Forbes India covered the summit’s sovereign model launches, with Business Standard counting three models unveiled on February 19 and Forbes India counting five new sovereign models. The counts differ because the outlets grouped releases differently, and we flag that rather than pick a winner. The November framing from ET Government sits on top of that groundwork. It treats foundation models as the base layer and applications as the product. For readers who track the sector, the practical message is that grant money and political attention are tilting toward use cases in education, agriculture, health, banking and citizen services. ## What ET Government Reported and What We Could Confirm ET Government’s report ties the sovereign AI story to a named academic voice, Prof Ganesh Ramakrishnan of IIT Bombay, who is the principal investigator at BharatGen. Open-source ARTEX framework linked to espionage and financially motivated campaigns. ## Key points * China-linked group VAPOR PANDA used the open-source ARTEX framework to target more than 200 organisations worldwide in under a fortnight, CrowdStrike said. * ARTEX acts as a harness wrapping tools around large language models such as DeepSeek, letting a human operator in Mandarin direct intrusions using roughly 1.4 billion input tokens. * GTIG's Rohit Nambiar called the campaign a warning shot from unsophisticated 'skids', noting there is no evidence fully autonomous, human-out-of-the-loop hacking exists yet. ![ARTEX AI hacking framework spreads to another China-linked group](https://i.nextmedia.com.au/Utils/ImageResizer.ashx?n=https%3a%2f%2fi.nextmedia.com.au%2fNews%2fartex.png&h=420&w=748&c=0&s=0) A China-linked hacking group used an open-source AI attack framework to target more than 200 organisations worldwide in less than a fortnight, security vendor CrowdStrike said. The security vendor [said](https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/vapor-panda-uses-artex-to-scale-global-campaign/) the group it tracks as VAPOR PANDA began using the ARTEX framework on October 17, targeting foreign ministries, United States semiconductor, defence and think tank organisations, and telecommunications providers across several regions. CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation activity at nine organisations, where attackers deployed a backdoor and conducted credential spraying, network scanning and reconnaissance. It is the latest of three prominent ARTEX campaigns publicly detailed by security researchers in October, following Microsoft's identification of the framework in attacks by China-aligned actor Storm-0940 and CrowdStrike's earlier discovery of its use [against South Korean financial institutions](https://www.reuters.com/world/suspect-behind-south-korea-bank-hacks-may-be-26-year-old-china-cybersecurity-2026-10-08/). CrowdStrike said the South Korean attacks were likely the work of a China-based individual rather than a confirmed state-linked group. ARTEX's developer, a GitHub user known as Autumn-27, withdrew the original code in October because of its misuse, Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant [said](https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/artex-and-friends-enter-agentic-offensive-frameworks). However, copies continue to circulate, including localised versions and a commercial edition called ARTEX PRO. **Harness with BYO model** ARTEX is not an AI model itself, but a harness. This is software wrapped around a large language model (LLM), giving it tools such as a command shell, a shared record of discoveries, and a planner that breaks an intrusion into tasks for multiple agents. Infra & Chips.content: ![Bei Akademie registrieren](/images/banner_desktop_1110x150.webp) ![ad-hoc-news.de](/img/logos/ad-hoc-news.svg) # [BÖRSE](/boerse/news) # [BÖRSE](/boerse/news) ![Logo ad-hoc-news.de](/img/logos/ad-hoc-news.svg) # Micro-Star International stock expands its AI infrastructure push ## AI Infrastructure Broadens MSI's Reach ![MSI, TW0002377009, Illustration mit AI erstellt.](https://mdb.ad-hoc-news.de/bild/bild-2405025_1200_0.webp) Micro-Star International presented a broader AI infrastructure portfolio at the OCP Global Summit on October 13, 2026. According to [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/msi-showcases-open-data-center-and-ai-infrastructure-at-2026-ocp-global-summit-ce785dd2db89f620 "MarketScreener report on MSI at the 2026 OCP Global Summit"), the company showcased 21-inch ORv3 systems, DC-MHS modular platforms, NVIDIA MGX rack and server solutions, and the XpertStation WS300 desktop AI supercomputer. The presentation gives investors a view of MSI's push beyond traditional gaming and PC components. Its infrastructure lineup is designed to cover different deployment sizes, from local AI development to high-density data center workloads. ## From Modular Servers To Desktop AI MSI's ORv3 portfolio includes two-node systems in air-cooled and direct-liquid-cooled configurations. The company also presented a 48-rack-unit NVIDIA MGX configuration built from liquid-cooled servers, networking equipment and management switches. The XpertStation WS300 extends the same strategy to the desktop. The system uses NVIDIA's GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip and supports local AI model prototyping, fine-tuning and inference. Two units can be clustered for larger workloads, according to the MarketScreener report. For investors, the product mix points to an attempt to capture AI infrastructure spending across several layers rather than relying only on consumer PC demand. Commercial adoption, customer orders and the pace of data center investment remain important factors for the outlook. ## MSI's Business And Competitive Position MSI is a Taiwan-based computer hardware company that manufactures and distributes motherboards, graphics cards, notebooks, monitors, servers, industrial computers and related consumer electronics. Its products are sold mainly in Taiwan, Europe, other parts of Asia and the Americas, according to the company profile published by MarketScreener and [MSI](https://www.msi.com/about/investor "MSI investor information"). In PC components and gaming hardware, MSI competes with Taiwan-based ASUSTeK Computer and Gigabyte. MSI is positioned as a diversified specialist that combines consumer hardware with a growing server and AI infrastructure offering, while its rivals have similarly broad positions across PC components and systems. ### Micro-Star International At A Glance Regional technology shares remain sensitive to demand for computing hardware and AI infrastructure; see [Current market reports](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/marktberichte/). Infra & Chips.titleZh: ASUS Unveils AI Server XA P2N-E2 - Inven Global
Infra & Chips.content: # [Inven Global](/) ## ASUS Unveils AI Server XA P2N-E2 ![Byungho ](https://static.invenglobal.com/upload/image/2017/05/19/i1495184226821987.jpeg) [Byungho "Haao" Kim](https://www.invenglobal.com/author/byungho-haao-kim/articles) [haao@inven.co.kr](mailto:haao@inven.co.kr) [Korean (한국어) KO](https://www.inven.co.kr/webzine/news/?news=322839 "View in Korean") [Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=invenglobal.com) [![에이수스, AI 서버 XA P2N-E2 공개](https://static.invenglobal.com/upload/image/2026/11/02/i1793582226329827.jpeg)](https://static.invenglobal.com/upload/image/2026/11/02/i1793582226329827.jpeg) ⓒ ASUS ASUS Korea (hereinafter ASUS) unveiled the XA P2N-E2 AI server for the first time at the OCP Global Summit 2026 held in San Jose, California. Powered by NVIDIA Vera CPUs, the 2U server is targeted at agentic AI and reinforcement learning workloads. Based on the NVIDIA MGX architecture, the XA P2N-E2 combines CPU computing and GPU acceleration features, supporting up to two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. Its processing targets extend beyond AI model inference to the core execution layer of applications, including code execution, sandboxing, and data processing. ASUS explained that the server was designed to maintain the responsiveness of AI agents even during complex execution and evaluation tasks through high single-thread performance and high-bandwidth, low-power memory. The event's exhibits ranged from individual servers to rack-scale AI systems, networking, context memory, ultra-low-latency inference, and high-density storage. The rack-scale XA VR721-E3 integrates 36 NVIDIA Vera processors and 72 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs on the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platform. It features a fully liquid-cooled architecture designed for large-scale AI training and inference. Servers featuring hybrid cooling methods were also on display. The XR R1I12B-M1BHFS applies Direct-to-Chip Liquid Cooling to the GPU baseboard chips based on NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8, while air-cooling the Intel Xeon 6 processors. ASUS explained that this design enables flexible server configurations. For infrastructure based on the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, ASUS presented a combination of four core technologies. Alongside the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8, it showcased the NVIDIA Spectrum-6 Ethernet switch for high-speed AI networking, NVIDIA CMX for scalable context memory storage, and the NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX for accelerating token-generation inference in agentic systems. The server lineup for cloud, AI, and HPC included platforms based on Intel and AMD processors. Powered by Intel Xeon 6, the RS700-E12-RS4U and RS720-E12-RS12U are 1U and 2U dual-socket platforms, respectively. Both products incorporate the DC-MHS architecture and a tool-less maintenance design to support modular deployment and data-intensive workloads. The AMD-based RS700A-E14B-R16U was introduced as a 1U dual-socket platform equipped with 6th Gen AMD EPYC 9006 Series processors (code-named Venice). It supports the PCIe 6.0 interface and up to 16 E3.S drives, leveraging ASUS Thermal Radar 3.0 technology for thermal management. For AI acceleration, ASUS also exhibited the ESC8000A-E13P supporting AMD Instinct MI350P, alongside the XA AM3A-E13, which integrates eight AMD Instinct MI355X accelerators into a 10U form factor. ASUS plans to supply key new products, including the XA P2N-E2, as well as its AI infrastructure portfolio, to markets worldwide. Infra & Chips.content: * [United States](/news/us) * / * [IT](/news/us/it) * / * NasdaqGS:AKAM # Akamai Stock In Focus After New AI Services Launch [Simply Wall St](/news/about-simply-wall-st-news) Reviewed by[Sasha Jovanovic](/news/about-simply-wall-st-news/sasha-jovanovic) * Akamai Technologies recently launched Akamai Inference and Akamai Agent Sandbox, giving enterprises managed access to open-weight and custom AI models, secure agent execution, and AI-optimized infrastructure on Akamai Cloud, supported by NVIDIA GPU clusters and OpenAI-compatible APIs. * The new AI stack positions Akamai Technologies to monetize its global network and high-end GPU fleet by hosting customer models, agents, and data pipelines in one integrated environment. This development could influence how its cloud infrastructure and security businesses evolve. * We will now examine how Akamai’s new Inference service, with OpenAI compatible APIs, could shape the broader investment narrative. Scan beyond Akamai Technologies and line up other AI infrastructure plays by reviewing the curated [54 AI infrastructure stocks](https://simplywall.st/discover/investing-ideas/473744/ai-infrastructure-stocks/global) that could benefit from similar heavy investment in GPUs and model hosting capacity. Advertisement ## Akamai Technologies Investment Narrative Recap To own Akamai Technologies you need to believe the shift from a shrinking delivery segment to higher value security and Cloud Infrastructure Services can support the business while capital intensity climbs. The recent launch of Akamai Inference and Akamai Agent Sandbox fits that story, but on its own it does not materially change near term drivers. The key near term catalyst remains execution on large AI infrastructure and security contracts while keeping non GAAP operating margins around management’s mid 20s target. The biggest risk is simple: heavy CapEx tied to AI workloads and concentrated CIS customers may not scale to the cash gross margin profile Akamai is aiming for. Infra & Chips.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![사이언스모니터 | The Science Monitor](https://scimonitors.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/t-logo.png)](https://scimonitors.com/en/) [![사이언스모니터 | The Science Monitor](https://scimonitors.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/t-logo.png)](https://scimonitors.com/en/) ![FuriosaAI’s 3.8 Trillion Won Valuation: State Funds, No Chip Allies](https://scimonitors.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/f.jpg) [Asia](https://scimonitors.com/en/category/world-en/asia-china-en/) | [Politics & Policy](https://scimonitors.com/en/category/policy-en/) | [World](https://scimonitors.com/en/category/world-en/) # FuriosaAI’s 3.8 Trillion Won Valuation: State Funds, No Chip Allies By[David](https://scimonitors.com/en/author/davic/) ## A 3.8 trillion won valuation, a cliff in actual sales and the risk of investors cashing out ## Isolated from direct strategic equity alliances with global chip giants ## Sidelined from the AI chip and memory supply-chain ecosystem, where structural limits meet distortions of state-directed finance Korean artificial intelligence (AI) chip fabless (design-only) startup FuriosaAI wrapped up a Series D round totaling 820 billion won (about $620 million) in late October 2026, reaching a post-money valuation of 3.8 trillion won (about $2.9 billion). That is nearly four times the valuation it received in its Series C bridge round in July 2025 ($735 million, about 1 trillion won), a surge achieved in just one year and three months. Major foreign media such as Bloomberg reported that FuriosaAI had secured a large war chest for its pursuit of Nvidia. Yet comparing the details of its investor list (cap table) with the financial statements in its audit reports reveals structural limits where the cold reality of the global semiconductor ecosystem intersects with the distortions of state-directed finance. The most unusual and central point of criticism in this round is that the disclosed shareholder list shows no direct strategic investment (SI) from global or Korean chip giants. Because survival in the AI chip industry hinges on securing allocation at leading-edge foundry processes, a stable supply of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and reference customers in global cloud data centers, it is regarded as an industry where equity alliances with core companies in the semiconductor value chain, such as Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, Arm, Marvell and Nvidia, are essential. However, while rivals such as Rebellions, Tenstorrent, d-Matrix and Groq have opened up both supply chains and sales channels on the back of strategic investments from global chip and cloud giants, FuriosaAI’s 820 billion won raise was completed with state and policy funds, including the National Growth Fund (a government-led fund for strategic industries, 370 billion won), the state-run Korea Development Bank (30 billion won) and the Export-Import Bank of Korea (a state export-credit lender), shouldering about half, and domestic and foreign financial investors (FIs) filling the rest. Taken together with the controversy before the Series D over an early financial investor’s sale of 50 billion to 60 billion won in existing shares (a possible “peak-out” signal), the cold shoulder from Korea’s venture capital (VC) industry, the debate over the real-world inference performance of its flagship second-generation chip RNGD (Renegade), and the supply-chain risk of a third-generation roadmap that would mount 12 HBM4 stacks per chip without a memory maker among its shareholders, it is hard to avoid concerns that the current valuation is an overvaluation created by the government’s “K-Nvidia” promotion drive rather tha...
